title: Anju Devi v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Ajit Kumar and Siddharth Nandan, JJ.
disposition: Petition disposed of; petitioner directed to raise Clause 6.5 objections; respondent No. 4 to decide after meter inspection.
headnote: Writ seeking correction of an allegedly excessive electricity bill disposed of with a direction that the consumer raise objections under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks, grant the department full access for meter reading and inspection, and that respondent No. 4 consider and decide the objections within one month after the meter is checked. The bill was not examined on merits.
facts: Anju Devi filed a writ petition under Article 226 seeking amendment of an electricity bill raised by the Electricity Department, alleging it was excessive. Counsel for the department submitted that whenever the departmental team visited the premises where the meter is installed, the petitioner was never found available, so meter reading could not be taken and no further action could be taken on the bill.

holding_units.holding: A writ petitioner seeking correction of an allegedly excessive electricity bill is to raise objections under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (here, within two weeks). If objections are raised, the departmental team may visit the premises; the consumer shall provide full access for taking the meter reading and inspecting the meter. After the meter is checked, the concerned officer shall consider and decide the objections (here, within a further one month).

not_decided.point: Whether the electricity bill was in fact excessive.
